title: Optimal Calibration of Quantum Network Links
authors: Vinay Kumar, Claudio Cicconetti, Marco Conti, Andrea Passarella
abstract: The reliable distribution of entanglement is essential for the effective operation of quantum networks. Due to fundamental differences between quantum and classical communication systems, it is necessary to develop specialised algorithms and protocols that also account for quantum-specific constraints. In this work, we focus on the issue of recalibration. As suggested by recent experimental studies, the process of local entanglement generation in a quantum link degrades over time due to environmental changes that have to be estimated and compensated via a calibration operation, during which the link is not available. Therefore, in such a quantum network, every link alternates between an activation period, during which it operates normally, and a calibration period, during which it cannot participate in the end-to-end entanglement distribution, thereby creating a trade-off between link quality (the fidelity of generated pairs, which decays during activation) and availability (the fraction of time the link is usable, which calibration reduces). We develop analytically a protocol for optimally assigning activation periods to each link in linear quantum repeater chains, subject to any general end-to-end fidelity requirements and local initial fidelity thresholds. Building on this foundation, we extend to general quantum networks, where multiple paths may cross at common links, proposing a heuristic approach evaluated in simulations and compared with a benchmark, numerical approach, and theoretical bounds.
summary: This paper develops optimal scheduling protocols to manage the trade-off between link quality and availability in quantum networks. By modeling fidelity decay over time, it derives analytical solutions for simple chains and proposes advanced heuristics for complex topologies. The work is crucial for designing robust, high-throughput quantum communication infrastructure.
main_problem: The core problem is developing an optimal scheduling protocol for quantum network links that balances link quality (fidelity, which decays over time) against availability (which is reduced by necessary calibration downtime). This must be done to maximize overall end-to-end throughput.
main_result: For linear chains, the paper derives analytical protocols (QLO) showing optimal scheduling based on fidelity thresholds. For general networks, it proposes heuristics (MIN/GRO) due to non-convex optimization challenges.
method: The work employs network optimization theory, transforming time-dependent fidelity decay into log-fidelity space ($L$-space). It uses analytical derivations for linear chains and heuristic/numerical approaches for complex topologies.
model_or_system: The system is a quantum network composed of links (modeled as optical fibers) connecting quantum repeaters. Entanglement distribution requires periodic recalibration to counteract environmental drift, creating an operational trade-off.
key_observables: End-to-end fidelity ($F_{ete}$), effective throughput ($T$), and the required activation/calibration time periods ($a_e$ vs $c$).
important_parameters: Individual link fidelity thresholds ($L_{th, e}$) and the global end-to-end fidelity constraint ($L$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes exponential decay of fidelity with activation time. For general networks, the objective function becomes non-convex, necessitating heuristic approximations.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate fidelity decay curves (showing single/stretched exponentials) and allowed regions in fidelity space ($	ext{F}_{m0}$ vs $	ext{F}_{m1}$) that define feasible operating points for maximum throughput.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from characterizing link degradation via experiment (polarization drift), to developing optimal scheduling for simple linear chains using analytical theorems, and finally extending the methodology to complex, shared-resource general quantum networks using heuristics.
why_interesting: It provides a rigorous mathematical framework for resource allocation in realistic quantum communication channels, directly addressing the operational limitations of current quantum network designs by integrating maintenance downtime into the core optimization loop.

The ✓in the figure means the successful delivery of an entangled pair across the network, while × denotes an unsuccessful attempt due to probabilistic failure of entangled pair generation on either or both of the links involved.

The green and blue blocks correspond to the activation and calibration periods, respectively, of physical link e.
